volatilitySection.title: Volatility-Based Analysis
volatilitySection.desc: Compares portfolios near the target volatility based on price series covariance and cash limits.
volatilitySection.desc2: LOW/MID/HIGH are not absolute risk grades but relative to each card's target volatility.

efficiencySection.title: Efficiency-Based Analysis
efficiencySection.desc: Compares portfolios with higher risk-adjusted efficiency, considering both expected return and volatility.
efficiencySection.desc2: Current return (avg cost) is for reference only and is not used in analysis.

theoreticalCard.cashMaxDesc: Achievable when holding more cash than the current cash limit.
theoreticalCard.addCashDesc: Requires additional capital beyond current holdings.

marketAnalysis.title: Market-Based Analysis
marketAnalysis.desc: Examines how the final expected flow was determined combining historical and market-based flow.
marketAnalysis.footnote: Market-based analysis adjusts the final expected flow by referencing how closely stocks moved with the market. Not a guaranteed return or recommended weight.

riskContribution.title: Risk Contribution
riskContribution.subtitle: Identify stocks contributing more risk than their portfolio weight.

overlayScenario.title: Overlay Scenarios
overlayScenario.desc: Sensitivity analysis based on supplementary observations that does not replace core risk optimization. Shows how selected overlays affect scaling the current portfolio. Not recommended weights or optimal returns.

capmSection.title: CAPM · SCL · SML E[R] Blend
capmSection.desc: The optimization input E[R] blends historical flow estimate and CAPM expected return, weighted by confidence based on sample size, benchmark quality, and explanatory power.
capmSection.blendDesc: Blends historical flow E[R] and CAPM E[R] using confidence-based weights.
capmSection.capmWeightNote: CAPM weight is calculated reflecting common sample size, benchmark quality, missing rate, R², correlation, and volatility stability.

capmWeightFactors.commonSample: Common sample: increases as the number of common return samples grows.
capmWeightFactors.benchmarkSource: Benchmark source: higher for stored or externally supplemented data.
capmWeightFactors.coverage: Data coverage: higher as the benchmark missing rate decreases.
capmWeightFactors.rSquared: Market explanatory power (R²): higher as market returns better explain stock returns.
capmWeightFactors.correlation: Correlation: higher as the co-movement between stock and benchmark strengthens.
capmWeightFactors.volatility: Volatility stability: reduces CAPM weight when stock volatility is excessively high.
capmWeightFactors.historicalWeight: Historical weight: increases as CAPM confidence decreases.

sclSection.title: SCL Diagnostics
sclSection.noData: Insufficient common return observations to draw SCL regression.

legend.points: Blue dots: daily log returns on common trading days

sclSection.regressionDesc: {{benchmark}} basis · Stock return = daily α + β × Benchmark return
sclSection.footnote: SCL is a supplementary diagnostic summarizing the relationship between daily log returns of benchmark and stock.

smlSection.title: SML Diagnostics
smlSection.footnote: SML is a supplementary diagnostic showing stock positions relative to the CAPM line; not a guaranteed return or recommended weight.

frontier.title: Efficient Frontier
frontier.desc: E[R] is an annualized estimate blending historical flow with market-based expected returns, weighted by confidence.
frontier.ariaLabel: Efficient frontier, capital allocation line, and investor indifference curve
frontier.tooltipRfLabel: Shown at CAL off-axis end in chart
frontier.efNote: Chart E[R] is capped at -30%~60% for visual stability. Pre-cap expected returns are used in calculations.

markerBasis.frontier: The efficient frontier is the upper boundary of min-variance portfolios at each target return for 100% risky assets, with dominated points removed.
markerBasis.maxSharpe: The max-Sharpe portfolio maximizes (E[R] - r_f) / σ on the efficient frontier. The line through this point from the risk-free asset is the reference CAL.
markerBasis.riskAllocation: CAL risk allocation blends the max-Sharpe risky asset combo with the risk-free asset, adjusting the risky weight based on risk-aversion γ and cash limit.
markerBasis.utilityOptimal: The utility-optimal portfolio maximizes U = E[R] - 0.5 · γ · σ². With current constraints applied, it sits at the closest feasible boundary when the theoretical tangent is outside constraints.
markerBasis.theoreticalUtility: The theoretical utility point is where CAL and indifference curve are tangent without constraints. Computed as y* = (E[R]_maxSharpe - r_f) / (γ · σ_maxSharpe²).
markerBasis.minVol: The min-variance portfolio minimizes wᵀΣw for 100% risky assets. The covariance structure matters more than expected returns.
markerBasis.indifference: The investor indifference curve is a σ-E[R] set with equal utility U. It is tangent to the CAL at the interior solution.
markerBasis.current: The current portfolio is calculated from user-entered quantities, avg costs, and cash. Unrealized P&L is display-only; price series returns/covariances are used in optimization.
markerBasis.cal: The CAL extends from the risk-free rate r_f toward the max-Sharpe portfolio. Extended as a dashed line past max-Sharpe when a theoretical utility point exists.

frontier.indifferenceCurveNote: The indifference curve is rendered to pass through the utility-optimal portfolio based on actual risk-aversion γ {{gamma}}.

theoreticalAdvanced.title: Theoretical Utility Point
theoreticalAdvanced.cashMaxDesc: The unconstrained tangent at γ requires a higher cash ratio than the current cash limit. Relaxing the limit makes this point achievable.
theoreticalAdvanced.addCashDesc: The unconstrained tangent at γ requires more risky asset capital than current total assets. Additional investment makes this point achievable.
